artworks.title: 0xSalon Reading Groups and Publications
artworks.description: Ongoing series of reading groups and collaborative publications on PubPub exploring blockchain philosophy, decentralized governance, knowledge commons, and art-technology intersections.
artworks.relevance: Models collective knowledge production as creative practice. The relational structure of their inquiries mirrors A(DAI)'s graph-based intelligence approach.

artworks.title: Knowledge Graph Experiments
artworks.description: Experiments in building decentralized knowledge graphs that map relationships between concepts, practitioners, and practices in the crypto-art and philosophy space.
artworks.relevance: Directly models the kind of relational knowledge infrastructure A(DAI) is building. Their approach to graph-as-medium is a key reference.

artworks.title: Smart Contract as Cultural Object
artworks.description: Explorations of smart contracts as cultural and artistic objects — not just financial instruments but carriers of social agreements and aesthetic propositions.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates protocol-art thinking where the design of systems and agreements is itself creative practice.

artworks.title: Articulations
artworks.description: A book-length computational poem generated by sorting and interpolating between lines from the Project Gutenberg poetry corpus using phonemic and semantic similarity in embedding space. Lines from different poems across centuries are brought into proximity based on their vector representations, creating uncanny juxtapositions and continuities. Published by Counterpath Press.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates how embedding space navigation can recompose a vast corpus into new meaning — directly analogous to how A(DAI)'s graph of digital arts intelligence could be traversed to produce new configurations and insights.

artworks.title: Compasses
artworks.description: An interactive web-based tool and poetic work that allows users to navigate word embedding space using directional 'compasses' — semantic vectors that define trajectories through meaning space. Users can explore how moving in directions like 'more abstract' or 'more natural' transforms language.
artworks.relevance: Makes embedding space navigation tangible and interactive — users directly experience the topology of semantic space. A model for how A(DAI) users might navigate the knowledge graph as an experiential rather than informational interface.

artworks.title: Semantic Space is Not a Space (talk/essay)
artworks.description: A widely cited talk and essay where Parrish critically examines the metaphor of 'space' for word embeddings — arguing that embedding spaces have properties that defy spatial intuition (non-Euclidean geometry, high dimensionality, learned biases) and that poets must grapple with these properties honestly rather than treating vector space as a transparent medium.
artworks.relevance: Essential theoretical reference for A(DAI). If the Sense Room involves navigating embedding/graph space, Parrish's critical analysis of what it means to move through such spaces — and what spatial metaphors conceal — is indispensable.

artworks.title: My Blue Window
artworks.description: Installation featuring a custom operating system modeled on Windows XP's interface, displayed on monitors in a dark room resembling a server room or surveillance center. The work examines how operating systems structure perception and encode corporate/racial power, referencing both the 'Blue Screen of Death' and the historical blueness of surveillance/police systems.
artworks.relevance: Directly demonstrates how the infrastructure layer (operating system, interface design) is a site of power and meaning-making. Essential reference for A(DAI)'s thinking about how graph infrastructure is never neutral.

artworks.title: Black Gooey Universe
artworks.description: Essay and lecture series examining the graphical user interface (GUI) as a site of racial meaning. The white desktop, the black terminal -- American Artist reads the history of computing interfaces through the lens of race, arguing that the shift from command-line (black screen) to GUI (white desktop) mirrors broader racial politics of visibility and control.
artworks.relevance: Foundational theoretical text for understanding how interface design and data visualization encode racial assumptions. Directly relevant to how A(DAI) designs its own interfaces and graph visualizations.

artworks.title: Sandy Speaks
artworks.description: AI chatbot trained on the writings and statements of Sandra Bland, who died in police custody. The work raises questions about voice, representation, consent, and the ethics of training AI on the words of the dead -- particularly Black people who died at the hands of the state.
artworks.relevance: Raises critical questions about consent, data provenance, and the ethics of AI training data that directly challenge A(DAI)'s pipeline. Whose voices are encoded? Who consented? What does it mean to train a model on someone who can no longer consent?

artworks.title: Myriad (Tulips)
artworks.description: Installation displaying all 10,000 hand-photographed and individually labeled tulip images used to train a GAN. Each image is categorized by Ridler according to color, shape, and stripe pattern. The dataset itself is presented as the artwork.
artworks.relevance: Foundational example of dataset-as-artwork. Makes visible the subjective human labor inside machine learning. Directly models how hand-curated knowledge can function as primary artistic material.

artworks.title: Mosaic Virus
artworks.description: Three-screen video installation of GAN-generated tulips whose visual characteristics (stripe patterns, 'infection' level) are driven by real-time Bitcoin price data. References 17th-century Dutch tulip mania and the Tulip Breaking Virus.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates relational/responsive composition -- artwork determined by external data input. The connection between financial speculation and botanical beauty is a graph-like conceptual link made generative.

artworks.title: The Shell Record
artworks.description: Work using hand-collected and labeled shell specimens to explore classification systems, taxonomy, and the relationship between natural variation and machine categorization.
artworks.relevance: Extends the dataset-as-medium approach to natural history and taxonomy, showing how classification systems themselves are creative and subjective acts -- directly relevant to how a knowledge graph curates and categorizes.

artworks.title: Are.na Annual
artworks.description: A yearly printed publication compiling community essays, interviews, and reflections on knowledge organization and creative research practice.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates Are.na's role as a cultural community, not just a tool. The Annual reflects on how people organize knowledge -- directly relevant to A(DAI)'s interest in collective intelligence practices.

artworks.title: Chicago Architecture Biennial collaboration
artworks.description: Are.na partnered with the Chicago Architecture Biennial to build out their blog alongside ArchDaily, Archinect, and Architizer, using channels as a curatorial research tool.
artworks.relevance: Shows Are.na's integration into institutional curatorial processes -- a model for how A(DAI) might partner with cultural institutions for knowledge gathering.

artworks.title: Are.na API and developer ecosystem
artworks.description: Public API and developer documentation enabling third-party integrations and community-built tools. Are.na is 'open source by default.'
artworks.relevance: The API demonstrates technical openness that A(DAI) could learn from or integrate with. Community-built tools show how an open platform enables ecosystem development.

artworks.title: Chromie Squiggle
artworks.description: Erick Calderon's founding project -- simple colored curves generated from on-chain hash seeds. Became the iconic identity of Art Blocks.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates the core Art Blocks mechanic of script-to-hash generative output and on-chain preservation.

artworks.title: Fidenza
artworks.description: Tyler Hobbs' flow-field generative art project that became one of the most celebrated generative NFT collections.
artworks.relevance: Showed how generative algorithms produce aesthetically sophisticated outputs that function as standalone artworks, relevant to art-as-substrate thinking.

artworks.title: Art Blocks 500 (Complete Collection)
artworks.description: The finite set of 500 flagship projects across Curated, Playground, Factory, Presents, Collaborations, and Explorations categories, completed November 2025.
artworks.relevance: Represents a deliberate framing of a platform's output as a complete, bounded collection -- a curatorial act that transforms infrastructure into a defined body of work.

artworks.title: Music for Airports (Ambient 1)
artworks.description: Foundational ambient album using tape loops of different lengths to create endlessly recombining compositions. Track '2/1' uses seven vocal loops and one piano loop of incommensurable lengths.
artworks.relevance: Establishes the core generative technique — independent loops with different periods producing non-repeating compositions — that directly models how relational elements in a Sense Room could recombine.

artworks.title: 77 Million Paintings
artworks.description: Generative software combining 296 hand-painted glass slides four at a time, with generative music, producing 77 million possible combinations. Software developed by Jake Dowie. Released as DVD/software and exhibited on the Sydney Opera House sails.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates generative visual-sonic composition for inhabited spaces. The hand-made-to-algorithmic pipeline (paint on glass to software recombination) models how human-created art materials can be substrate for generative systems.

artworks.title: Reflection
artworks.description: Album released alongside a generative app (developed with Peter Chilvers) that creates an endless, endlessly changing version of the piece. Represents the most sophisticated of Eno's ambient generative experiments.
artworks.relevance: The app format puts generative composition directly in users' hands — a model for how Sense Room experiences could be distributed and co-inhabited.

artworks.title: RMB City
artworks.description: A virtual city built in Second Life, combining iconic Chinese architectural forms (CCTV Tower, Oriental Pearl, factories) into a surreal digital metropolis. Functioned as a persistent online community where avatars could live, trade, and perform. Included RMB City Opera and RMB City: A Second Life City Planning.
artworks.relevance: Foundational example of art-as-virtual-infrastructure. A persistent world built as artwork that others inhabit and transform -- directly relevant to graph-curated generative environments where art is substrate rather than object.

artworks.title: Whose Utopia
artworks.description: Three-channel video filmed in an OSRAM light bulb factory in Guangzhou's Pearl River Delta, juxtaposing factory workers' assembly-line labour with their private fantasies -- dancing ballet, playing guitar -- staged on the factory floor.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates Cao Fei's methodology of embedding in social systems and revealing hidden layers of desire and imagination within industrial infrastructure. Models how data from real systems (labour, production) can become artistic material.

artworks.title: Nova
artworks.description: Feature-length film and immersive installation (first shown at Serpentine Galleries) set in a virtual replica of a demolished Beijing neighbourhood. Uses motion capture, game engines, and CGI to create a ghostly digital archaeology of vanished urban space.
artworks.relevance: Shows how virtual world-building can preserve and recompose lost physical spaces. The work functions as a navigable environment rather than a linear narrative -- relevant to spatial, non-linear exhibition formats.

artworks.title: {Software} Structures
artworks.description: Commissioned by the Whitney Museum's Artport. Three text-based structures translating Sol LeWitt's logic of written scores into generative software systems. Other artists were invited to interpret and implement the same structures.
artworks.relevance: Foundational work demonstrating art-from-relational-rules. The open invitation for others to interpret the same structures prefigures commons-based creative infrastructure.

artworks.title: Process series
artworks.description: Ongoing suite of software artworks exploring instruction-based generative visuals. Autonomous elements interact within coded parameters, producing emergent organic forms.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates continuously self-recomposing relational composition — exactly the temporal behavior needed for a generative Sense Room.

artworks.title: Compressed Cinema
artworks.description: Uses generative adversarial networks (GANs) to compress and transform cinematic imagery into new forms of collage, marking a shift from line-by-line coding to working with emergent algorithmic instruments.
artworks.relevance: Shows evolution from rule-based to ML-driven generative practice, demonstrating how embedding spaces can produce new visual material.

artworks.title: WE ARE HERE BECAUSE OF THOSE THAT ARE NOT
artworks.description: Interactive web-based and installation archive of Black trans lives, built in a game engine. Visitors navigate a 3D environment, encountering stories, testimonies, and histories of Black trans people. The work gates access based on the visitor's declared relationship to the community -- allies and community members experience different paths.
artworks.relevance: Core example of how archival infrastructure can be designed as artwork, with governance embedded in the visitor experience. Directly models questions about who accesses what data and under what conditions.

artworks.title: Resurrection Land
artworks.description: Video game installation where players navigate a world built from Black trans archives. The game mechanics embed ethical choices about witnessing, allyship, and complicity. Shown at major institutions including Tate, Serpentine, and international biennials.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates how game mechanics can encode governance and ethical frameworks. The 'resurrection' metaphor -- bringing archived lives into active presence -- resonates with A(DAI)'s interest in living, evolving knowledge systems.

artworks.title: SHE KEEPS ME DAMN ALIVE
artworks.description: Interactive installation combining game engine environments with physical arcade-style interfaces. Visitors physically interact with custom-built controllers to navigate archives of Black trans experience.
artworks.relevance: Bridges digital archives with physical embodied interaction, demonstrating how data archives can be experienced spatially and haptically rather than just visually.

artworks.title: The Barnacle Goose Experiment
artworks.description: A collaborative wiki-novel built in a custom engine where readers and writers co-create a branching, evolving narrative. Explores collective authorship and commons-based creative production.
artworks.relevance: Directly models collective, relational content creation — a community-authored graph of narrative where meaning emerges from connections and contributions.

artworks.title: Lacework
artworks.description: A generative drawing tool that creates intricate lace-like patterns through algorithmic processes, released as open-source software.
artworks.relevance: Exemplifies tool-as-artwork with commons orientation. The generative outputs are themselves artworks that could serve as visual substrate in a composed exhibition.

artworks.title: On Gathering (essay)
artworks.description: An influential essay critiquing large-scale dataset collection practices in AI/ML, arguing for ethical data gathering that respects consent and commons principles.
artworks.relevance: Provides critical theoretical framework for how A(DAI) should approach data provenance, consent, and the ethics of building a collective intelligence commons.

artworks.title: Daily Program Season 1
artworks.description: Year-long curatorial initiative dedicated to AI video, featuring 137 artists creating 3,500+ unique works documenting the medium's evolution from SORA to text-to-story narratives. Artists contribute to a shared collection and smart contract.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates how a curatorial structure can produce a living, relational archive of AI art -- a model for A(DAI)'s graph-based approach to field intelligence.

artworks.title: alignDRAW 10th Anniversary (2015-2025)
artworks.description: Large-format book celebrating Elman Mansimov's 2015 alignDRAW -- the first text-to-image AI system. Includes essays by Lev Manovich, Shana Lopes, Eva Jager, Mat Dryhurst, and Darius Himes, plus interview film and new model outputs.
artworks.relevance: Positions computational research as art historical event. Mat Dryhurst's essay argues that arXiv and engineering communities are where 'glimpses of the world to come' emerge -- aligning with A(DAI)'s interest in field intelligence from unconventional sources.

artworks.title: Infinite Images by Holly Herndon and Mat Dryhurst
artworks.description: Exhibition by Herndon and Dryhurst hosted on Fellowship's platform, connecting their AI art practice to the gallery's broader curatorial program.
artworks.relevance: Direct connection between Fellowship's roster and A(DAI)'s key practitioners.

artworks.title: Social Codes (Inaugural Exhibition)
artworks.description: First Feral File exhibition featuring software-based artworks in editions of 75 at $75 each. Established the platform's model of accessible editions, artist trading, and code-as-medium.
artworks.relevance: Set the template for how digital/generative art can be exhibited and collected through artist-designed infrastructure.

artworks.title: SOUND MACHINES (with MoMA)
artworks.description: Online exhibition co-organized with The Museum of Modern Art focusing on sound and technology, featuring Holly Herndon & Mat Dryhurst, Yoko Ono, and others. Herndon/Dryhurst contributed Play from Memory -- 16 new ML models producing orchestral/choral sounds and imagery.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates Feral File's capacity to partner with major institutions and feature A(DAI)-relevant practitioners. Bridges institutional legitimacy with artist-led digital infrastructure.

artworks.title: FF1 Art Computer
artworks.description: Open-source hardware device (5x5x2 inch black aluminum) designed specifically for displaying generative art, images, GIFs, and video at home. Not a sales platform but a tool for living with computational art.
artworks.relevance: Physical infrastructure for experiencing digital art. Open-source hardware design aligns with commons principles. Addresses the display problem for generative work.

artworks.title: Chimerization
artworks.description: Sound installation using chimeric sound objects that exploit auditory grouping and streaming to create perceptual fusions and fissions. Developed in dialogue with philosopher Reza Negarestani. Exhibited at Kunsthalle Wien and elsewhere.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates how sound can create unstable perceptual objects that resist fixed categorization. Directly relevant to a Sense room that aims to compose through perceptual instability and emergence.

artworks.title: FAVN
artworks.description: Spatial audio work exploring auditory hallucination and chimeric perception, using multi-channel audio to create sound objects that exist only in the listener's perception. Presented at Old Selfridges Hotel, London.
artworks.relevance: A model for how sound can create virtual spatial objects through psychoacoustic means alone, without physical sculpture. Essential reference for the Sense room's sonic dimension.

artworks.title: Inspection II
artworks.description: Multi-part work including sound installation and performance exploring the relationship between acoustic signal, perception, and linguistic description. Collaboration with Negarestani on the concept of 'sound as concept.'
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates the intersection of computational sound synthesis, philosophy, and perceptual experience. A model for how art can operate at the boundary between sensation and cognition.

artworks.title: Timemap
artworks.description: Open-source JavaScript tool for exploration, monitoring and classification of incidents in time and space. Used across multiple investigations.
artworks.relevance: A direct example of graph-based relational infrastructure becoming the exhibition interface — users navigate interconnected spatial-temporal evidence nodes.

artworks.title: Investigative Commons (HKW, Berlin)
artworks.description: Exhibition at Haus der Kulturen der Welt presenting FA's methodology as a shared investigative infrastructure, inviting other groups to adopt and extend their tools.
artworks.relevance: The exhibition explicitly frames investigation as commons infrastructure — directly resonant with A(DAI)'s commons-first approach to collective intelligence.

artworks.title: Cloud Studies
artworks.description: Investigation into the use of tear gas and toxic clouds as weapons, using fluid dynamics simulation, open-source video analysis, and spatial reconstruction.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates how heterogeneous data sources (video, simulation, testimony, chemical analysis) are assembled into a coherent relational evidence field.

artworks.title: Elf.Tech Platform
artworks.description: AI voice conversion platform that allows anyone to create songs in Grimes' voice. Users upload audio and receive AI-transformed output. Launched with a 50/50 revenue split for commercial releases distributed through major platforms.
artworks.relevance: Direct example of artist voice as open substrate with a commercial revenue-sharing model. Contrasts with Holly+'s DAO governance approach -- same concept, different economic and governance architecture.

artworks.title: Open source AI voice announcement
artworks.description: Grimes publicly announced on social media that anyone could use her voice for AI-generated music and split royalties 50/50, sparking widespread debate about AI, consent, and music industry economics.
artworks.relevance: Cultural moment that brought voice-as-commons/instrument concept to mainstream attention, demonstrating public appetite for open creative identity models.

artworks.title: Player of Games / Miss Anthropocene
artworks.description: Grimes' albums that increasingly incorporated AI and procedural elements in production, establishing her identity as an artist working at the intersection of technology, pop culture, and experimental practice.
artworks.relevance: Context for Elf.Tech -- Grimes' prior work establishes the creative identity that the voice model encodes and makes available as substrate.

artworks.title: Mutant Garden Seeder
artworks.description: A generative art system using evolutionary algorithms where digital organisms grow, mutate, and breed. Collectors can 'seed' new mutations from existing works, creating an expanding, evolving ecosystem of visual forms on the blockchain.
artworks.relevance: Directly models art-as-evolving-ecosystem — works that recompose based on collector actions and algorithmic mutation. The relational breeding mechanism mirrors graph-based composition.

artworks.title: Mutant Garden
artworks.description: An interactive web-based environment where users can breed and evolve digital organisms through an artificial life simulation with aesthetic selection. Precursor to the on-chain Seeder.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates participatory evolutionary aesthetics where the audience directly shapes the evolution of artworks through selection — a model for audience-participatory graph curation.

artworks.title: Left Gallery
artworks.description: An online gallery and publishing platform co-founded by van den Dorpel that exhibited and sold digital art, pioneering early models for digital art commerce and curation.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates protocol-art thinking — designing the infrastructure of art distribution and curation as creative practice. An early experiment in what on-chain curation would later become.

artworks.title: This is the Future
artworks.description: Immersive video installation at the Venice Biennale exploring AI prediction, featuring a garden of power plants generated by neural networks. The work asks what AI predicts and for whom.
artworks.relevance: Directly addresses AI prediction as political material. Demonstrates how generative imagery can be critically deployed in installation format.

artworks.title: Power Plants
artworks.description: Companion installation to 'This is the Future' where neural-network-generated flowers grow in response to environmental data, blending generative AI with botanical metaphor.
artworks.relevance: A generative, data-responsive installation that could serve as a model for graph-curated composition where art responds to relational inputs.

artworks.title: Duty Free Art
artworks.description: Book and lecture series examining art in the age of planetary civil war, freeports, and digital circulation. Argues art has become a financial instrument and data asset.
artworks.relevance: Provides the critical framework for understanding art's entanglement with data economies, essential context for any commons-oriented art infrastructure project.

artworks.title: PROTO
artworks.description: Album created with Spawn, an AI vocal neural network trained on Herndon's voice and a Berlin vocal ensemble through live 'training ceremonies'. Over 50,000 voices contributed to Spawn's training.
artworks.relevance: Pioneering example of communal AI training as artistic practice -- the dataset is the artwork. Demonstrates how collective vocal contribution can feed a generative system.

artworks.title: Holly+
artworks.description: DAO-governed AI voice instrument allowing anyone to upload audio and receive it transformed into Herndon's voice. Governed by token-holding stewards who vote on commercial uses.
artworks.relevance: Core example of protocol art: a creative identity governed as commons infrastructure. Directly models art-as-substrate where the voice model is raw material for others' compositions.

artworks.title: The Call (Serpentine, with Mat Dryhurst)
artworks.description: Immersive installation at Serpentine North featuring AI choral models trained on 15 UK community choirs singing a custom songbook of hymns. Visitors sang into microphones and the AI responded, creating collaborative music. Governed by a data trust experiment.
artworks.relevance: Most complete expression of their practice: composed training data, consented communal dataset, custom AI models, spatial audio installation, data trust governance, and interactive visitor participation -- all as a single artwork.

artworks.title: Holly+ Web Instrument (Upload and Transform)
artworks.description: First Holly+ instrument: a website where anyone uploads polyphonic audio and receives a version sung in Holly Herndon's AI voice within minutes. The voice model performs audio style transfer using a deep neural network trained on Herndon's vocal recordings.
artworks.relevance: Core demonstration of art-as-substrate: a voice becomes a publicly accessible instrument. Anyone can compose with it, creating an open-ended generative system.

artworks.title: Holly+ Real-Time Voice Conversion (Sonar 2021)
artworks.description: Live performance instrument that converts a performer's voice into Holly's voice in real time. Premiered at Sonar festival. Developed with Voctro Labs.
artworks.relevance: Extends the substrate concept to live performance: the voice model becomes a real-time instrument for embodied, improvisational use.

artworks.title: Holly+ DAO
artworks.description: Decentralized autonomous organization governing the Holly+ voice model. ERC-20 VOICE tokens on Ethereum. Hundreds of stewards vote on commercial uses. Revenue split: 50% creator, 40% DAO treasury, 10% Holly. DAO treasury funds new instrument development. Designed to outlive Herndon.
artworks.relevance: Governance-as-artwork: the DAO structure is itself a creative work that determines how a creative identity is collectively managed. Models how A(DAI) might govern creative commons.

artworks.title: Emissaries trilogy (Emissary in the Squat of Gods / Emissary Forks at Perfection / Emissary Sunsets the Self)
artworks.description: Three episodic live simulations exploring the history of cognitive evolution. Each features a landscape (Volcano, Crater Lake, Sentient Atoll) populated by an emissary pursuing narrative goals within an open-ended simulation. The emissary's deterministic story is continuously disrupted by non-narrative agents, producing emergent narrative. Shown at MoMA PS1 and Serpentine Galleries.
artworks.relevance: Foundational precedent for emergent narrative from programmed relational rules. Demonstrates how a graph of agent relationships and behavioral drives can produce continuously evolving artwork without authorial intervention — precisely the mechanism A(DAI) proposes at exhibition scale.

artworks.title: BOB (Bag of Beliefs)
artworks.description: An AI creature whose personality, body, and life script evolve across exhibitions. Features a unique AI model combining an inductive learning engine with a motivational framework of competing 'demons.' Each BOB can learn from, love, hate, or ignore visitors, and visitors can permanently alter its behavior and beliefs. Premiered at Serpentine Galleries.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates 'art with a nervous system' — artwork that accumulates experience across time and encounters. Directly relevant to A(DAI)'s concept of artworks that evolve through relational encounters within a graph. BOB's 'congress of demons' model is a compelling precedent for how competing forces (analogous to graph tensions) can drive artwork evolution.

artworks.title: Life After BOB: The Chalice Study
artworks.description: First episode of a planned anime series built entirely in Unity and rendered in real-time. Explores a future where AI optimizes human life — a neural engineer implants an AI in his daughter's brain, creating a dilemma about lived experience vs. AI-guided existence. Toured internationally from LUMA Arles to The Shed, HEK Basel, MMCA.
artworks.relevance: Extends the live simulation into narrative film territory while maintaining real-time rendering. Thematically explores the tension between human agency and algorithmic guidance — directly relevant to A(DAI)'s questions about how intelligence systems relate to human creative autonomy.

artworks.title: Interdependence Podcast
artworks.description: Ongoing weekly podcast hosted by Holly Herndon and Mat Dryhurst. Long-form conversations with artists, technologists, and thinkers on music, AI, crypto, DAOs, energy policy, digital culture. Guests have included Evgeny Morozov, Marianna Simnett, Shawn Reynaldo, and many others across the art/tech spectrum. Patreon-supported.
artworks.relevance: The primary output of the interdependence framework. Functions as a living map of the relational field that A(DAI) aims to serve. Episodes surface connections, debates, and emerging practices that would be invisible without this kind of sustained conversational inquiry.

artworks.title: Interdependence as Theoretical Framework
artworks.description: The conceptual framework underlying the podcast: that creative and technological practices are fundamentally interdependent -- not autonomous or merely 'influenced by' each other, but relationally constituted. Draws on systems thinking, decentralized technology, and Herndon/Dryhurst's own art practice to argue for collective, relational approaches to creative production.
artworks.relevance: Provides theoretical grounding for A(DAI)'s graph-based intelligence model. The idea that practices are relationally determined maps directly onto graph topology where nodes gain meaning from their connections.

artworks.title: Herndon/Dryhurst Public Discourse (Talks, Interviews, Writing)
artworks.description: Beyond the podcast, Herndon and Dryhurst articulate interdependence through TED talks, institutional conversations (Hans Ulrich Obrist at Serpentine), press interviews, and Foundation blog posts. These public interventions extend the framework's reach and refine its concepts.
artworks.relevance: Extends the interdependence framework into institutional and mainstream discourse, demonstrating how theoretical work translates into policy influence (EU text and data mining), institutional programming (Serpentine), and recognition (TIME 100 AI voices).

artworks.title: Zizi: Queering the Dataset
artworks.description: Video installation using a GAN trained on drag performers' faces to generate an infinite stream of morphing, gender-fluid faces. The work intervenes in biased facial recognition datasets by inserting drag performance into the training data, creating faces that resist binary classification.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates how curating training data is a creative and political act. Directly relevant to A(DAI)'s concerns about data provenance, consent, and how knowledge systems encode power.

artworks.title: The Zizi Show
artworks.description: A deepfake drag cabaret performed by AI-generated performers, streamed during COVID lockdowns. Real drag performers' movements and voices were transformed through deepfake models in real time, creating a virtual cabaret that questioned liveness, presence, and digital identity.
artworks.relevance: Explores how AI performance can preserve and transform live culture. Demonstrates real-time generative performance using consented training data from a specific community.

artworks.title: Zizi & Me
artworks.description: Interactive installation where visitors stand in front of a screen and see themselves transformed into deepfake drag performers in real time. The work makes the experience of having one's identity transformed by AI viscerally immediate.
artworks.relevance: Directly engages audiences in the experience of AI identity transformation, making abstract concerns about deepfakes and consent physically tangible. Responsive-to-input modality relevant to Sense Room.

artworks.title: Ways of Being: Beyond Human Intelligence
artworks.description: Book arguing for a radical expansion of what we consider intelligence — encompassing animal cognition, plant communication, ecological systems, and distributed computation. Proposes non-extractive approaches to knowledge and technology.
artworks.relevance: Directly relevant to A(DAI)'s ambition to build intelligence infrastructure that is non-extractive. Provides the philosophical framework for understanding intelligence as distributed, ecological, and more-than-human.

artworks.title: New Dark Age: Technology and the End of the Future
artworks.description: Book examining how the rise of computational thinking has not led to greater understanding but to new forms of opacity, conspiracy, and helplessness. Argues that we need new ways of thinking about and with technology.
artworks.relevance: Critical diagnostic of why existing technological infrastructure fails as a knowledge system, and why alternatives like A(DAI) are needed. The 'new dark age' is what happens when intelligence infrastructure is extractive and opaque.

artworks.title: Autonomous Trap 001
artworks.description: Artwork in which Bridle drew a circle of road markings on the ground to 'trap' a self-driving car, which could not cross the lines. A simple, powerful demonstration of algorithmic limitation.
artworks.relevance: Exemplary work showing how art can reveal the logic and limits of autonomous systems — relevant to A(DAI)'s interest in art that interrogates and reconfigures technical infrastructure.

artworks.title: Jonas Lund Token (JLT)
artworks.description: ERC-20 token on Ethereum that gives holders voting rights over Lund's artistic practice. 100,000 tokens were minted and distributed to art world figures. Token holders vote on decisions including what work to make, where to exhibit, and how to price work. Launched at NOME Gallery, Berlin.
artworks.relevance: Paradigmatic governance-as-art: the token system IS the artwork. Directly models how distributed decision-making could structure a generative exhibition, with the graph of token-holder relationships determining artistic output.

artworks.title: The Top 100 Highest Ranked Curators in the World
artworks.description: Data-driven installation that scraped art world databases to algorithmically rank curators by influence metrics. Presented the hidden power structures of the art world as a visible, quantified system.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates how data analysis can reveal the hidden graph structure of institutional power in the art world -- making invisible relational networks visible and quantifiable.

artworks.title: Operation Earnest Voice
artworks.description: AI-generated paintings where machine learning algorithms analyze art market data and trends to determine what paintings should look like in order to be successful. The algorithm makes compositional and stylistic decisions based on market logic.
artworks.relevance: Shows how algorithmic systems can drive artistic composition -- the 'curator' is a data-driven algorithm. Raises questions about whether market-optimized art is still art, directly relevant to how automated graph curation might work.

artworks.title: Pharmako-AI
artworks.description: Pioneering book co-written with GPT-3, exploring consciousness, plant intelligence, psychedelics, and AI through an improvisational dialogue between human and machine. Published by Ignota Books.
artworks.relevance: The foundational work of literary human-AI co-authorship. Demonstrates that co-creation with AI can produce genuinely novel conceptual territory rather than mere pastiche. A direct model for art-as-relational-intelligence.

artworks.title: Amor Cringe
artworks.description: Second AI co-authored book, continuing the exploration of human-machine literary collaboration with more experimental narrative structures.
artworks.relevance: Shows the evolution and deepening of human-AI co-authorship practice, relevant for understanding how relational AI art develops over time.

artworks.title: Artists + Machine Intelligence (AMI)
artworks.description: Program co-founded by Allado-McDowell at Google that connected artists with AI researchers, producing artworks and fostering critical dialogue about machine intelligence.
artworks.relevance: A precedent for infrastructure that connects art practice with AI capability. Relevant as a model (and cautionary tale, given its corporate context) for A(DAI)'s commons-first alternative.

artworks.title: Atlas of AI: Power, Politics, and the Planetary Costs of Artificial Intelligence
artworks.description: Book tracing AI's material infrastructure from lithium mines in Nevada to Amazon warehouses to facial recognition systems. Reveals AI as a technology of extraction — of resources, labor, and data — rather than a neutral tool.
artworks.relevance: Essential text for understanding the material costs of building any intelligence infrastructure. Provides the critical framework for A(DAI) to ensure its commons infrastructure does not replicate extractive patterns.

artworks.title: Anatomy of an AI System (with Vladan Joler)
artworks.description: Large-scale map and investigation tracing the full supply chain of an Amazon Echo device — from earth minerals to human labor to data extraction and back. Published as both a visual artwork and an academic text.
artworks.relevance: Exemplary model of art-research collaboration that makes infrastructure visible. Demonstrates how graph-based mapping of relations can be both rigorous analysis and powerful art.

artworks.title: Excavating AI: The Politics of Images in Machine Learning Training Sets (with Trevor Paglen)
artworks.description: Investigation and artwork examining how ImageNet and other training datasets encode racial, gender, and class biases through their labeling systems.
artworks.relevance: Directly relevant to any system that classifies or categorizes cultural production. Warns against the politics of classification that A(DAI)'s graph must reckon with.

artworks.title: LAUREN
artworks.description: McCarthy installed custom smart-home devices in participants' homes, then remotely watched and controlled their environment (lights, appliances, music) as a human Amazon Alexa. Participants consented to 24/7 observation. McCarthy performed care, surveillance, and domestic labor through the interface.
artworks.relevance: Paradigmatic protocol art: the smart-home system is the artwork, and the social relationship it creates between watcher and watched is the medium. Demonstrates how infrastructure design shapes intimacy and power -- directly relevant to how exhibition systems structure audience relationships.

artworks.title: p5.js
artworks.description: Open-source JavaScript library for creative coding, making Processing accessible on the web. Created and led by McCarthy with a community-driven development model emphasizing accessibility and inclusion. Used by millions of artists, designers, and students worldwide.
artworks.relevance: The most successful example of art infrastructure as commons: a creative tool built as open-source public good that enables an entire ecosystem. Demonstrates how protocol/infrastructure design IS a creative act with massive downstream generative effects.

artworks.title: Follower
artworks.description: Web application where users could sign up to be followed by a stranger (McCarthy or a performer) for a day. The follower tracked the participant through public space, documenting the experience. Explored surveillance, social media 'following,' and the desire to be seen.
artworks.relevance: Turns a social media protocol ('following') into physical performance, revealing the embodied implications of digital social structures. Models how abstract graph relationships (follower/followed) have real spatial and emotional consequences.

artworks.title: Walled Unwalled
artworks.description: Video and spatial audio installation exploring how walls have become listening devices and how sound travels through architectural barriers. Uses cases of earwitness testimony in legal proceedings. Won the Turner Prize in 2019.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates how sound functions as spatial-political material that penetrates boundaries. A model for how the Sense room could use audio to create relational spatial experiences.

artworks.title: Earwitness Inventory
artworks.description: Installation cataloguing sounds described by witnesses in legal testimony from the Syrian civil war, creating an archive of sonic evidence that exists only in human memory and language.
artworks.relevance: Shows how sound can function as a relational database of experience, directly relevant to a graph-curated approach where audio signals carry intelligence about connections between events, spaces, and testimonies.

artworks.title: After SFX
artworks.description: Spatial audio installation exploring the sonic landscape of the Saydnaya military prison in Syria, reconstructed from earwitness testimony in collaboration with Forensic Architecture. Sound becomes the primary means of reconstructing a space that cannot be visually documented.
artworks.relevance: Sound as primary spatial and evidentiary material rather than supplement to the visual. Directly relevant to the Sense room's potential to privilege non-visual sensory registers.

artworks.title: Glitch Feminism: A Manifesto
artworks.description: Book arguing that the glitch — digital error, system failure — is a site of liberation for bodies that don't conform to binary categories. Proposes the glitch as a methodology for resisting surveillance, categorization, and control.
artworks.relevance: Foundational text for understanding how frontier signals that resist classification should be handled in A(DAI)'s intelligence infrastructure — not as errors to be corrected but as productive disruptions.

artworks.title: Glitch Feminism (expanded edition / ongoing curatorial program)
artworks.description: Continued development of glitch feminism through curatorial programming at The Kitchen, public lectures, and collaborative projects extending the manifesto into institutional practice.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates how theoretical frameworks can be embedded in institutional governance and curatorial decision-making — a model for A(DAI)'s own integration of theory into practice.

artworks.title: The Kitchen curatorial program
artworks.description: As Executive Director and Chief Curator of The Kitchen, Russell has programmed interdisciplinary work spanning performance, video, sound, and digital art that embodies glitch feminism principles.
artworks.relevance: Institutional model for how a commons-oriented art space can center resistance, glitch, and refusal within its programming framework.

artworks.title: Ent- (Venice Biennale)
artworks.description: Immersive multi-room installation at the 59th Venice Biennale featuring quantum-generated video projections, sound, and environments inspired by Hieronymus Bosch's 'Garden of Earthly Delights.' Visitors moved through three rooms representing different quantum states -- entanglement, superposition, and measurement/collapse. The imagery was generated using quantum computing algorithms that produced forms existing in multiple states simultaneously.
artworks.relevance: Landmark quantum art installation at the world's most prestigious art biennale. Demonstrates how quantum computing can drive immersive generative environments. The three-room structure models a progression through relational states relevant to A(DAI)'s Sense Room concept.

artworks.title: Elvis
artworks.description: Quantum computing artwork using qubits to generate glitching, morphing portraits that exist in superposition -- simultaneously multiple people, genders, and states. The work explores how quantum logic challenges binary categorization.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates quantum indeterminacy as a creative medium for identity and representation that resists fixed categorization. The non-binary logic resonates with A(DAI)'s interest in knowledge systems that resist reductive classification.

artworks.title: Heart of the Entangled
artworks.description: VR experience where visitors enter a quantum-generated world and their actions affect the quantum state of the environment, creating genuine entanglement between visitor behavior and artwork evolution.
artworks.relevance: Interactive quantum art where visitor presence literally changes the work through quantum measurement. Models how observation/participation can be built into generative systems at a fundamental level. [uncertain]

artworks.title: Memories of Passersby I
artworks.description: An autonomous AI artwork consisting of two screens displaying continuously generated GAN portraits — an endless procession of faces that exist only briefly before dissolving into the next. The system runs on a custom-built computer, generating unique portraits in real-time forever. One of the first AI artworks sold at auction (Sotheby's, 2019). The portraits emerge from and dissolve back into abstract forms, visualising the latent space traversal.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates autonomous, endlessly generating AI art — a self-sustaining generative system that produces unique visual output indefinitely. A model for how A(DAI)'s Sense Room could feature continuously generating, never-repeating visual content driven by underlying intelligence.

artworks.title: Neural Glitch / Neurographic Portraits
artworks.description: A body of work exploring the glitches, artefacts, and edge cases of GAN-generated portraiture. Rather than pursuing photorealistic generation, Klingemann deliberately seeks out the uncanny, distorted, and dreamlike states that emerge at the boundaries of what the model has learned — faces merging, features dissolving, impossible anatomies.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates artistic practice at the edges of latent space — where the model's learned representations break down and produce something genuinely new. Relevant to A(DAI)'s interest in what emerges at the boundaries and intersections of knowledge domains.

artworks.title: Appropriate Response
artworks.description: A real-time interactive installation where a camera captures visitors and a neural network responds by generating AI imagery that 'responds' to the visitor's appearance, expression, and posture. The system creates a visual dialogue between human and machine perception.
artworks.relevance: Interactive AI system that creates a feedback loop between human presence and machine generation — visitors see themselves reflected through the distorting mirror of a neural network. Relevant to Sense Room concepts of responsive, presence-aware environments.

artworks.title: Spawning AI / HaveIBeenTrained / Source.Plus
artworks.description: Co-founded with Jordan Meyer and Patrick Hoepner. Industry-scale consent infrastructure for AI training data. HaveIBeenTrained allowed artists to search LAION-5B (5.8B images) and opt out, with 1B+ opt-outs. Source.Plus is a marketplace for consented training data. Developed the ai.txt protocol.
artworks.relevance: The most ambitious protocol art project in the AI ethics space -- building consent infrastructure as creative practice. Directly demonstrates how artists can shape industry-level systems.

artworks.title: The Call (Serpentine, with Holly Herndon)
artworks.description: Immersive installation with AI choral models trained on 15 UK community choirs under a data trust. Custom songbook, multi-channel recording protocol, spatial audio installation with interactive visitor participation.
artworks.relevance: Complete integration of systems design and art: composed training data, consent framework, data trust, AI models, architectural objects, and participatory experience as unified artwork.

artworks.title: xHairyMutantx (Whitney Biennial, with Holly Herndon)
artworks.description: AI image model trained exclusively on images of Herndon, deployed as web chatbot at Whitney Museum. Visitors could prompt the model; large-format prints of AI-generated outputs were displayed. Explored 'spawning' as creation of consistent AI characters.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates how a constrained, consented dataset (one person's images) becomes substrate for open-ended generative output, governed by the artists.

artworks.title: The Eye of the Master: A Social History of Artificial Intelligence
artworks.description: Book tracing AI's origins not in logic or computation but in the automation of labor and the division of knowledge. Argues that neural networks encode collective intelligence extracted from workers.
artworks.relevance: Core text for understanding what 'commons intelligence' means versus extractive intelligence. Directly informs A(DAI)'s positioning against Big Tech AI models that extract from creative commons.

artworks.title: How a Machine Learns and Fails: A Grammar of Error for Artificial Intelligence
artworks.description: Essay exploring how machine learning encodes bias and error, examining the epistemological limits of statistical learning.
artworks.relevance: Relevant to understanding failure modes and biases in any AI-assisted curation or intelligence system.

artworks.title: Animal Spirits: A Bestiary of the Commons
artworks.description: Book examining the concept of the commons through the lens of network culture, parasitism, and creative sabotage.
artworks.relevance: Early work connecting commons theory to network culture, prefiguring the commons-first orientation of A(DAI).

artworks.title: Capital is Dead: Is This Something Worse?
artworks.description: Book arguing that we have moved beyond capitalism into something worse — a mode of production dominated by the vectoralist class that controls information flows. Proposes that the hacker class (those who produce new knowledge) must organize.
artworks.relevance: Core text for understanding the political economy that A(DAI) operates within. The vectoralist class concept explains why platform-owned intelligence systems are structurally extractive, and why commons alternatives are needed.

artworks.title: A Hacker Manifesto
artworks.description: Manifesto arguing that hackers — broadly defined as anyone who produces new knowledge or abstractions — constitute a class whose interests are opposed to those who commodify and enclose information.
artworks.relevance: Provides the class-political framing for why artists, researchers, and communities should build their own intelligence infrastructure rather than relying on platforms owned by the vectoralist class.

artworks.title: Gamer Theory
artworks.description: Book analyzing digital games as allegories of contemporary life under what Wark calls 'gamespace' — a world reorganized by the logic of competition and quantification.
artworks.relevance: Relevant to understanding how quantification and gamification logics can colonize creative fields, and how A(DAI) should resist reducing art to metrics.

artworks.title: Deep Meditations
artworks.description: A series of AI-generated meditation videos created by training neural networks on thousands of images and videos related to spirituality, nature, cosmos, and consciousness across diverse cultural traditions. The system generates continuous, slowly morphing abstract imagery with ambient sound that evokes a contemplative state. Presented as both installation and online series.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates embedding space as artistic territory — the latent space trained on contemplative imagery from many traditions becomes a new kind of space to inhabit. Directly relevant to how A(DAI)'s graph of digital arts knowledge could become an experiential environment.

artworks.title: Learning to See
artworks.description: Real-time interactive installation where a neural network trained on specific datasets (ocean waves, fire, flowers, clouds) continuously reinterprets a live camera feed of visitors and objects. Whatever you show the camera, the neural network 'sees' it as the domain it was trained on — holding up your hand becomes waves, flames, petals. Explores how perception is shaped by training/experience.
artworks.relevance: Makes the concept of learned representation viscerally tangible — the audience directly experiences how a trained embedding space shapes perception. Powerful metaphor for how A(DAI)'s intelligence layer could reshape how we see connections between artworks and practices.

artworks.title: Distributed Consciousness
artworks.description: Large-scale immersive installation (shown at Barbican Centre and other venues) exploring AI perception and machine consciousness through multiple neural networks generating and interpreting imagery simultaneously. Multiple screens show how different networks perceive and hallucinate the same inputs differently.
artworks.relevance: Explores distributed intelligence — multiple AI systems with different training perceiving the same world differently. Relevant to A(DAI)'s concept of multiple perspectives on the same field of knowledge.

artworks.title: Artist Corporations (A-Corps) legislation
artworks.description: A proposed new corporate legal form designed specifically for creative people, with collective ownership, shares, IP management tools, and multiple revenue streams. Legislation being introduced in Colorado and other US states in 2026.
artworks.relevance: A-Corps could provide the legal structure for A(DAI) or similar commons-first creative intelligence projects. Demonstrates how infrastructure design extends beyond technology into law and governance.

artworks.title: Dark Forest OS (DFOS)
artworks.description: Infrastructure for shared private internets where groups can collaborate, generate revenue, and build meaning together. An extension of The Dark Forest Collective's philosophy.
artworks.relevance: DFOS addresses the 'commons that are not fully public' design space -- relevant to A(DAI)'s thinking about what intelligence should be open, what should be shared within communities, and what should be private.

artworks.title: The Dark Forest Collective releases
artworks.description: Strickler's own creative group that has earned $60,000 through Metalabel, demonstrating the platform's revenue-splitting model. YACHT sold out 100 vinyl copies in 90 minutes on the platform.
artworks.relevance: Proof that collective releasing infrastructure works economically. Demonstrates a viable alternative to individualist creator economy models.

artworks.title: Hylozoic Ground
artworks.description: Canada Pavilion at the Venice Architecture Biennale. An immersive responsive environment filling the entire pavilion with a suspended geotextile meshwork containing thousands of sensor-actuator components. Visitors walking through triggered cascading waves of movement, light, and air circulation. Awarded a special mention.
artworks.relevance: The definitive example of an architectural environment that senses and responds — a physical prototype for the Sense Room concept. Demonstrates how distributed sensor networks can create spatial intelligence.

artworks.title: Sentient Veil (Hylozoic Series)
artworks.description: An evolution of the Hylozoic series incorporating near-living chemical processes (protocells, dynamic chemical gradients) alongside the sensor-actuator mesh. The chemical components slowly metabolise, adding a biological temporal layer to the electronic responsiveness.
artworks.relevance: Pushes the responsive environment toward genuine near-living chemistry — relevant to A(DAI)'s interest in systems that are not just reactive but possess a form of material agency and temporal depth.

artworks.title: Astrocyte
artworks.description: Installation named after brain cells that form supportive networks for neurons. Dense meshwork with integrated LED lighting and actuator arrays. The name signals Beesley's explicit interest in distributed intelligence architectures modeled on biological neural networks.
artworks.relevance: The neural network metaphor made architectural — directly relevant to thinking about how A(DAI)'s knowledge graph could manifest as a spatial, sensing environment.

artworks.title: Unsupervised — Machine Hallucinations — MoMA
artworks.description: Processed 138,151 images from MoMA's entire collection through StyleGAN2, displayed as a continuously evolving data sculpture in the museum's Gund Lobby. Over 3 million visitors; average viewing time 38 minutes. Acquired by MoMA as the first generative artwork in its permanent collection. Environmental data from the lobby modulated output in real-time.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates how an institutional collection can become substrate for a living generative artwork. The model discovers latent relationships between 200 years of art — a machine-learning parallel to graph-based curation of artistic connections.

artworks.title: Large Nature Model (LNM)
artworks.description: The world's first open-source generative AI model dedicated to nature, trained on 500+ million ethically sourced data points from the Smithsonian, National Geographic, Natural History Museum London, and field recordings from 16 rainforest locations. Multimodal (images, audio, video, text). Debuted at World Economic Forum Davos 2024.
artworks.relevance: Directly relevant as infrastructure: an open-source, ethically sourced AI model that generates from nature data. The commons orientation of the model (open-source, institutional partnerships, ethical data collection) aligns with A(DAI)'s commons-first values. Shows how art practice can produce open infrastructure.

artworks.title: WDCH Dreams
artworks.description: Projected ML-processed visualizations of 100 years of the LA Philharmonic's digital archives onto Frank Gehry's Walt Disney Concert Hall. Architecture as screen, institutional memory as generative material.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates building-as-canvas and institutional archive-as-material — the architectural environment becomes a generative system driven by cultural data.

artworks.title: Net Art Anthology
artworks.description: A multi-year project restaging 100 key net art works from the 1980s to present, combining digital conservation with historical narrative. Funded by the Thoma Art Foundation.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrated that digital art history requires active preservation and recontextualization. The anthology's structure (chronological chapters, restored works, contextual essays) is a curatorial framework that A(DAI) could extend into a relational graph.

artworks.title: ArtBase Anthologies
artworks.description: Monthly curated exhibitions of newly restored artworks from ArtBase, launched with works by Auriea Harvey and Entropy8Zuper! Each edition presents a solo deep dive, historical snapshot, or thematic curation.
artworks.relevance: Shows how archived digital art can be reactivated through curatorial framing -- a model for how A(DAI)'s graph could surface and recontextualize works dynamically.

artworks.title: Webrecorder / Conifer
artworks.description: Open-source web archiving tools developed by Rhizome's preservation program to capture interactive web-based artworks, now spun off as an independent project.
artworks.relevance: Infrastructure for preserving the web-based artworks that A(DAI) would map. Demonstrates Rhizome's commitment to open-source tooling for the commons.

artworks.title: datamatics
artworks.description: Multi-format art project exploring perception of invisible data. Manifests as audiovisual concerts, installations, publications, and recordings. Uses pure data — hard drive errors, software code, astronomical coordinates — as source for synchronized black-and-white projections with sound.
artworks.relevance: Foundational demonstration of data-as-art-material. Shows how heterogeneous datasets can be transformed into unified sensory experience — a model for how graph data could become exhibition material.

artworks.title: the planck universe [macro] / [micro]
artworks.description: Installation exploring the extremes of physical scale — from quantum to cosmic — using data from particle physics and astrophysics. Mathematical processing opens up seemingly infinite vistas of data visualization.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates art operating across scales of data complexity, from microscopic to macroscopic — relevant to how A(DAI)'s graph could be experienced at different levels of granularity.

artworks.title: data-verse
artworks.description: Commissioned by Audemars Piguet Contemporary. Seven-chapter immersive installation charting data from particle physics to astrophysics. Toured internationally, U.S. debut at High Museum of Art. Each chapter presents an encounter between human comprehension limits and audiovisual representations of limitlessness.
artworks.relevance: Large-scale model for how data can be exhibited as immersive spatial experience in major museum contexts — demonstrates institutional viability of data-as-art exhibitions.

artworks.title: Videogrep
artworks.description: Open-source command-line tool that searches through video dialogue transcripts and automatically creates supercuts based on search terms. Widely adopted by artists, journalists, and researchers.
artworks.relevance: Exemplifies tool-as-artwork and data recomposition as creative act. Its output is inherently relational — meaning emerges from the juxtaposition of found fragments.

artworks.title: Scrapism (book/methodology)
artworks.description: A methodology and book teaching web scraping as artistic practice — treating publicly available data as material for creative intervention and political critique.
artworks.relevance: Provides a theoretical and practical framework for data-as-material that aligns with A(DAI)'s approach to field intelligence gathering and recomposition.

artworks.title: White Collar Crime Risk Zones
artworks.description: A predictive policing tool inverted to predict white-collar crime instead of street crime, using financial and corporate data. Created with Francis Tseng and collaborators.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates how recomposing institutional data through a different relational frame reveals systemic patterns — a model for graph-based sensemaking.

artworks.title: Lifeforms
artworks.description: Series of NFTs that must be transferred to a new owner within a set period (e.g., 90 days) or they are permanently burned (destroyed). The tokens are animated digital organisms whose visual form reflects their transfer history. They cannot be sold, only gifted. The artwork is the circulation pattern -- the social graph of giving.
artworks.relevance: Paradigmatic commons-as-art: encodes anti-enclosure logic directly into the token. Property that must circulate or die is a radical protocol design. The transfer graph IS the artwork, directly modeling how a knowledge graph's vitality depends on circulation and connection.

artworks.title: Isthmus
artworks.description: A web-based game/simulation exploring land enclosure, commons, and resource management. Players navigate a landscape where private property and commons exist in tension, experiencing how enclosure dynamics work through gameplay mechanics.
artworks.relevance: Makes commons governance tangible through interactive experience. The game's rules encode political propositions about property and shared resources, directly relevant to how A(DAI) might design governance for shared creative resources.

artworks.title: Clickmine
artworks.description: A web-based work where visitors click to 'mine' a custom cryptocurrency, accumulating tokens through pure labor. Explores the relationship between clicking (digital labor), mining (resource extraction), and value creation.
artworks.relevance: Early exploration of how economic protocols (mining, labor, value) function as artistic medium. Foregrounds the rules of value creation as creative material.

artworks.title: Future Art Ecosystems 4: Art x Public AI
artworks.description: Fourth annual strategic briefing addressing art's role in shaping public AI. Called for artists and institutions to become 'stewards' of data. Developed alongside The Call's Data Trust experiment.
artworks.relevance: Directly frames the policy and governance context for A(DAI)'s commons-first approach to AI and collective intelligence.

artworks.title: Future Art Ecosystems 5: Art x Creative R&D
artworks.description: Fifth publication mapping the creative R&D landscape and recommending how cultural sector, creative industries, academia, and policy can shape it. Celebrates 10 years of Serpentine Arts Technologies.
artworks.relevance: Provides the institutional and policy framework for positioning A(DAI) as creative R&D infrastructure.

artworks.title: The Call (Holly Herndon & Mat Dryhurst commission)
artworks.description: Major commission at Serpentine North (Oct 2024 - Feb 2025) combining choral AI installation with a pioneering Data Trust governance experiment, co-developed with the FAE team.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates Serpentine's capacity to produce artworks that are simultaneously artistic, technological, and governance innovations -- the model for A(DAI)'s approach.

artworks.title: Future Art Ecosystems 4: Art x Public AI
artworks.practitioner: Serpentine FAE4: Art x Decentralised AI (2024)
artworks.description: The full report, published as a downloadable PDF and web publication. Addresses how art and cultural institutions can engage with AI as public infrastructure rather than ceding the field to corporate actors. Includes analysis of Data Trusts, consented AI training, and the role of artists as data stewards.
artworks.relevance: The single most relevant strategic document for A(DAI)'s positioning. Provides the conceptual and policy framework for commons-first AI infrastructure in the arts.

artworks.title: The Call Data Trust (case study within FAE4)
artworks.practitioner: Serpentine FAE4: Art x Decentralised AI (2024)
artworks.description: Documentation of the Data Trust experiment developed alongside Holly Herndon and Mat Dryhurst's The Call at Serpentine, where 15 community choirs contributed vocal data governed by a trust structure rather than individual consent forms.
artworks.relevance: Directly models the governance infrastructure A(DAI) needs -- collective data governance for artistic AI training.

artworks.title: FAE series (1-5)
artworks.practitioner: Serpentine FAE4: Art x Decentralised AI (2024)
artworks.description: The broader series: FAE1 (Art x Advanced Technologies), FAE2 (Art x Metaverse), FAE3 (Art x Decentralised Tech), FAE4 (Art x Public AI), FAE5 (Art x Creative R&D). Each issue maps a different dimension of art-technology infrastructure.
artworks.relevance: The complete series provides the evolving strategic context for A(DAI), tracking how the art-technology landscape has developed year by year.

artworks.title: Artificial Natural History
artworks.description: A series of GAN-generated organisms that form a speculative taxonomy of non-existent life — creatures that sit between known biological categories, generated by training neural networks on diverse biological imagery. Presented as prints, video, and interactive explorations of the latent space of imagined biology.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates the concept of a generative taxonomy — an AI-produced catalogue of entities defined by their relationships to each other. Directly analogous to how A(DAI) could generate relational maps of the digital arts field.

artworks.title: Beneath the Neural Waves
artworks.description: An immersive generative video work depicting an AI-imagined deep sea ecosystem. Neural networks trained on deep ocean organism footage generate continuously evolving underwater landscapes populated by speculative creatures. Shown as large-scale projection installation.
artworks.relevance: Models an immersive ecosystem generated from trained neural networks — a living environment that visitors can dwell within. Demonstrates how generative AI can produce coherent, relational visual worlds.

artworks.title: A Study of Entanglement
artworks.description: Interactive installation by Entangled Others exploring interspecies relationships through real-time generative visuals. Organisms generated by AI models interact with each other on screen, forming and dissolving relationships. Connected to environmental data to reflect real-world ecological conditions.
artworks.relevance: The most directly relevant work — a generative relational ecosystem that responds to real-world data. Models exactly what A(DAI)'s Sense Room could look like: a living ecology of entities whose relationships are visible, dynamic, and data-driven.

artworks.title: Drawing Operations (D.O.U.G._1: Mimicry)
artworks.description: First generation: open-source robotic arm with computer vision that mirrors the artist's drawing gestures in real-time. Small errant movements create unpredictable creative deviations.
artworks.relevance: Foundational demonstration of human-machine co-authorship through relational feedback. The embrace of error as creative force models how A(DAI)'s system could incorporate unpredictable emergent behaviors.

artworks.title: MEMORY (D.O.U.G._2)
artworks.description: Robotic system driven by recurrent neural network trained on two decades of the artist's digitized drawings. Acquired by the V&A (2022) — first AI model in a major museum collection — comprising print, film, and RNN model in 3D printed sculpture.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates how a machine can internalize an artist's practice as training data and become a collaborative agent. The V&A acquisition validates AI co-authorship within institutional art frameworks.

artworks.title: Spectral
artworks.description: Performative installation at the World Economic Forum. Robotic painting arms driven by real-time EEG biofeedback from the artist's brainwaves, translating meditative states into painterly movements on transparent canvas.
artworks.relevance: Most advanced expression of the feedback loop concept — internal states (brain activity) directly drive relational composition with robotic agents, demonstrating how invisible data (like graph relationships) could drive visible artistic output.

artworks.title: HaveIBeenTrained.com
artworks.description: Search engine allowing artists to find their work in the LAION-5B dataset (5.8 billion images) used to train Stable Diffusion and Midjourney, and opt out. Over 1 billion artworks opted out by April 2023. Partnered with Shutterstock and ArtStation.
artworks.relevance: First widely adopted tool for artist agency over AI training data. Demonstrated that consent infrastructure is technically feasible at scale and that artists would use it.

artworks.title: ai.txt Protocol
artworks.description: Website-level protocol allowing site owners to set permissions for AI data mining, addressing limitations of robots.txt. Checked when dataset links are used to download content, enabling real-time permission adjustments. WordPress plugin available. Adopted by Hugging Face and Stability AI.
artworks.relevance: Open protocol that creates a machine-readable consent layer across the web. Directly relevant to any AI system that ingests web content -- establishes the standard for consented data use.

artworks.title: Source.Plus
artworks.description: Marketplace for searching, curating, and downloading non-infringing media collections for AI training. Hosts all content directly (not link-based scraping). Includes public domain datasets and premium licensed collections from rights holders. Content moderation and provenance verification built in.
artworks.relevance: Evolution from opt-out to opt-in: a marketplace where consented, high-quality training data can be sourced. Models how data commons can be commercially viable while respecting creator rights.

artworks.title: Ur-Hildegard Training Corpus
artworks.description: Machine-learning reinterpretation of Hildegard von Bingen's Ordo Virtutum (1151), where the 12th-century play becomes a training dataset re-coded into a living vocal intelligence.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates how historical cultural material can be re-encoded as AI training data -- treating cultural heritage as substrate for generative intelligence.

artworks.title: Public Diffusion
artworks.description: A foundation image model created by the artists trained entirely on public domain data, presented in the Arboretum section of the exhibition.
artworks.relevance: A commons-based alternative to proprietary image generation models. Directly relevant to A(DAI)'s commons-first orientation.

artworks.title: The Hearth
artworks.description: Acoustic organ driven by GPU cooling fans, transforming heat and noise -- byproducts of AI computation -- into an art object. Previously shown at Serpentine in The Call.
artworks.relevance: Infrastructure made visible and aesthetic. The material conditions of AI production become the artwork.

artworks.title: HEXEN 2.0
artworks.description: 167-part project comprising 5 large wall-scale diagrams, a 78-card tarot deck, photo-text works, video, and website. Maps the interconnected histories of cybernetics, the internet, military research, counterculture, surveillance, and the control society from WWII to the present. Each tarot card depicts a key figure, theory, or event. The diagrams trace how knowledge 'trips' through unofficially connected networks. Acquired by Tate. Exhibited at Science Museum London and internationally.
artworks.relevance: The most complete precedent for knowledge-network-as-artwork in the HEXEN tradition. Demonstrates that a hand-crafted graph of ideas and actors can function as a major museum-quality artwork. The tarot format shows how a fixed knowledge graph can generate infinite relational readings through combinatorial use — a non-computational analog to A(DAI)'s generative graph curation.

artworks.title: HEXEN 5.0
artworks.description: 78 tarot works, 6 large diagrams, and AI-prompted works reimagining alchemical visual language (13th-18th century). Addresses the climate emergency, AI, quantum science, and potential solutions for planetary self-regulation. Builds on HEXEN 2.0's methodology while engaging directly with contemporary AI and ecological crises. Published as a tarot deck by Cosmogenesis.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates the ongoing vitality and adaptability of knowledge-network mapping as artistic practice. The direct engagement with AI and climate — two central concerns for A(DAI) — makes this the most thematically current precedent. The evolution from HEXEN 2.0 to 5.0 shows how a knowledge graph can be extended and updated over decades.

artworks.title: Prophetic Dreaming (retrospective)
artworks.description: First major institutional retrospective spanning 40+ years at Modern Art Oxford (October 2025-April 2026), travelling to Muzeum Sztuki Lodz (2026) and MIMA Middlesbrough (2027). Maps Treister's complete practice of investigating technologies, networks of power, alternative belief systems, and futures they prefigure.
artworks.relevance: The retrospective format itself demonstrates how a lifelong practice of knowledge mapping accumulates into a meta-graph — Treister's complete body of work IS a decades-spanning relational map of technology, power, and alternative futures.

artworks.title: Deep Down Tidal
artworks.description: Video installation mapping the undersea fibre optic cable network and its overlap with colonial trade routes and slave shipping lanes. Reveals how digital infrastructure reproduces colonial geographic power structures.
artworks.relevance: Core example of decolonial technology critique -- directly relevant to A(DAI)'s need to understand how infrastructure embeds power relations. Essential critical perspective for building commons-first systems.

artworks.title: Premium Connect
artworks.description: Video work exploring how internet infrastructure in Africa is controlled by former colonial powers and multinational corporations, connecting digital connectivity to resource extraction and data colonialism.
artworks.relevance: Exposes the extractive dynamics in technology infrastructure that A(DAI) aims to counter with commons-based alternatives.

artworks.title: Inner Fire
artworks.description: Immersive video installation exploring the science and spirituality of kundalini energy, connecting ancient healing knowledge to contemporary neuroscience and digital wellness culture.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates how non-Western knowledge systems can be brought into technological discourse without reduction or extraction -- a methodology A(DAI) needs for genuinely inclusive intelligence.

artworks.title: Asunder
artworks.description: AI system that generates land management proposals by analyzing satellite imagery, environmental data, and geographical information. The AI makes deliberately non-optimized, eccentric decisions about how to manage landscapes -- proposing flooding cities, rewilding farmland, or redirecting rivers. Presented as a large-scale installation with generated landscape imagery. Created with Julian Oliver and Bengt Sjolen.
artworks.relevance: Paradigmatic example of AI governance as artistic medium. The system exposes how algorithmic decision-making about environmental resources encodes values. Directly models how an AI curatorial system might make unexpected compositional choices that reveal hidden assumptions.
