artworks.title: Eccentric Engineering
artworks.description: Series of installations creating alternative water treatment and environmental management systems that follow non-optimized, eccentric logics. Real functioning systems that clean water or manage ecosystems using unconventional approaches (e.g., a fish-controlled water treatment system).
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates how infrastructure design is a creative act -- the engineering decisions about how a system works encode specific values about efficiency, ecology, and governance. Directly relevant to how A(DAI)'s infrastructure design is itself a creative/political act.

artworks.title: Smell Dating
artworks.description: Matchmaking service that pairs people based on body odor rather than algorithmic profiling. Participants wore t-shirts for three days, then smelled samples to choose matches. Created with Sam Lavigne.
artworks.relevance: Subverts data-driven matching algorithms by using embodied, non-digital information. Exposes how dating platform infrastructure shapes social outcomes -- protocol critique through alternative protocol design.

artworks.title: The Hearth
artworks.description: Acoustic organ built from GPU cooling fans arranged like a pipe organ, filling the gallery with AI-generated hymns. At the organ's centre is an engraving of an infant blowing a lur (ancient wind instrument). Transforms computational infrastructure's byproducts into musical installation.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates how infrastructure itself (GPU fans, heat, noise) becomes artistic material -- directly relevant to A(DAI)'s interest in infrastructure as creative medium.

artworks.title: The Wheel
artworks.description: Spherical chandelier-like installation in the South Powder Room with gilded panels engraved with imagery from the recording tour, serving as symbolic centre for the choral data.
artworks.relevance: Physical manifestation of a data provenance record -- the journey of data collection made visible as sculptural object.

artworks.title: Oratory (Interactive Choral AI)
artworks.description: Interactive installation where visitors contribute their voices and the choral AI model harmonizes them in real-time, creating an experience akin to joining a choir.
artworks.relevance: Live demonstration of human-AI collective composition, where individual contributions are woven into a collective output -- core A(DAI) Sense Room principle.

artworks.title: Trust Reading Groups
artworks.description: Ongoing series of collectively organized reading groups on topics spanning technology, philosophy, politics, and ecology. Each series is carefully designed with curated reading lists and structured discussion formats.
artworks.relevance: Models how structured collective study can be a creative practice. The curatorial work of selecting texts and designing discussion formats mirrors A(DAI)'s graph curation.

artworks.title: Relearn
artworks.description: A recurring self-organized learning event/summer school exploring alternatives to conventional education, often involving Trust members. Participants propose and lead sessions on technology, art, and politics.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates decentralized, commons-based learning infrastructure. The self-organizing format models how A(DAI)'s community might contribute to and reshape the knowledge graph.

artworks.title: Trust Publications and Web Presence
artworks.description: Web-based publishing projects documenting reading groups, discussions, and collective research outputs. The website itself is a designed knowledge commons.
artworks.relevance: Shows how web infrastructure can embody commons values while functioning as a persistent, navigable knowledge resource.

artworks.title: New Extractivism
artworks.description: A cartographic project comprising a large-scale map, a manual, and a video animation that guides viewers through the 'traps, tunnels, and slippery corridors' of world-scale extractive infrastructure. Organized in 33 chapters exploring power, control, digital labor, colonialism, and exploitation of nature. Exhibited internationally including at Aksioma, Ars Electronica, and Warsaw Biennale.
artworks.relevance: The most direct precedent for graph-as-exhibition in A(DAI). Demonstrates that a relational diagram can function as a major artwork — the map IS the exhibition. The 33-chapter structure shows how graph-organized knowledge can be navigated as aesthetic experience. Available at extractivism.online as a web-native work.

artworks.title: Anatomy of an AI System
artworks.description: Collaboration with Kate Crawford (AI Now Institute, NYU). A large-scale map and long-form essay investigating the human labor, data, and planetary resources required to build and operate an Amazon Echo. Visualizes three extractive processes: material resources, human labor, and data. Won 2019 Design of the Year Award (Design Museum London), S+T+ARTS Prize Honorary Mention. In permanent collections of MoMA, V&A, Design Museum, Ars Electronica Center.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates how a single relational diagram can achieve major institutional recognition as artwork. The exploded-view methodology — tracing a consumer object back through its entire supply chain of materials, labor, and data — is a model for how A(DAI) could trace art-world phenomena through their full relational context.

artworks.title: Invisible Infrastructures (SHARE Lab)
artworks.description: A series of data investigations using network topology, data mining, and data visualization to create atlases of internet architecture, social media power structures, and algorithmic transparency. The first investigation mapped the physical infrastructure of the internet.
artworks.relevance: Establishes the methodology of infrastructure-mapping-as-art. SHARE Lab's investigative approach — combining technical analysis with critical visualization — is a model for how A(DAI) could investigate and visualize the digital arts field's own infrastructure.

artworks.title: The Question Concerning Technology in China: An Essay in Cosmotechnics
artworks.description: Hui's foundational work proposing the concept of cosmotechnics: the unification of the cosmic and the moral through technical activities. Argues that Chinese thought offers a fundamentally different relationship to technology than the Western Promethean tradition.
artworks.relevance: Provides the philosophical basis for understanding why technology must be culturally situated and why a single universal model of AI/technology is inherently extractive. Essential theoretical infrastructure for A(DAI).

artworks.title: Recursivity and Contingency
artworks.description: Explores how recursive systems (including algorithms, AI, and cybernetics) relate to contingency and freedom. Argues that understanding recursivity is key to developing non-deterministic approaches to technology.
artworks.relevance: Directly relevant to how generative systems in the Sense room might operate: through recursion that preserves contingency rather than deterministic algorithms that close down possibility.

artworks.title: Art and Cosmotechnics
artworks.description: Collection of essays exploring how cosmotechnics relates to art practice, aesthetics, and the possibility of non-Western technological aesthetics. Published by e-flux / University of Minnesota Press.
artworks.relevance: The most directly relevant work to the Sense room project: explicitly addresses how art practice can embody cosmotechnical thinking and how aesthetics relates to culturally situated technology.

artworks.title: alignDRAW 10-Year Anniversary Book
artworks.description: Large-format publication featuring essays by Lev Manovich (media theory, art history context), Mat Dryhurst (arXiv as site of cultural production), Eva Jager (institutional and curatorial perspective), Shana Lopes (art history), and Darius Himes (photography and image-making). Includes original alignDRAW outputs from 2015 and new generations.
artworks.relevance: Directly models A(DAI)'s approach: treating technical research as field intelligence and building relational narratives that connect engineering, art, and culture.

artworks.title: alignDRAW Exhibition at Art Basel Miami Beach
artworks.description: Exhibition presenting the alignDRAW book and related materials at Art Basel Miami Beach, positioning the project within the premier international art fair context.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates how field intelligence (a 2015 arXiv paper) can be exhibited in the highest tier of the art market, validating the canonisation methodology.

artworks.title: alignDRAW at Worcester Art Museum
artworks.description: Museum exhibition bringing the alignDRAW project into an institutional collection context, bridging from art fair to museum.
artworks.relevance: Shows the institutional pipeline from research artefact to art fair to museum collection -- a canonisation pathway A(DAI) can learn from.

artworks.title: fx(hash) 2.0 (Multi-chain launch)
artworks.description: Relaunch as a multi-chain platform bridging Tezos and Ethereum, breaking down barriers between blockchain ecosystems for generative artists.
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates how infrastructure design decisions (which chains to support) shape artistic communities and economic possibilities. Relevant to A(DAI)'s thinking about infrastructure as a form of governance.

artworks.title: FXH Protocol / Art Coins
artworks.description: Launch of the $FXH token on Base and art coins system, where ERC-20 tokens are linked to art collections via bonding curves, creating a new on-chain art economy with artist-owned liquidity.
artworks.relevance: Radical experiment in protocol art -- designing economic mechanisms as creative infrastructure. The bonding curve graduation model is a form of system design that determines how art gains and distributes economic value.

artworks.title: fx(hash) Tezos-era permissionless collections
artworks.description: The original permissionless Tezos platform where any artist could publish generative work without curation board approval, producing tens of thousands of generative art projects.
artworks.relevance: Showed that permissionless generative art infrastructure produces a different ecosystem than curated models -- more experimental, more accessible, more chaotic. Relevant to A(DAI)'s interest in commons vs. gatekeeping models.

artworks.title: teamLab Borderless
artworks.description: A museum without a map where artworks move out of rooms, communicate with and influence each other, and intermingle without boundaries. 1.55 million visitors in first anniversary year at new location. Selected by TIME as World's Greatest Places 2024.
artworks.relevance: Direct precedent for graph-curated exhibition — artworks as nodes whose relationships determine the visitor experience. The absence of fixed boundaries between works mirrors graph-based relational composition.

artworks.title: teamLab Planets
artworks.description: A museum where visitors physically immerse themselves in artworks, walking through water with responsive projections. Guinness World Record as most visited museum by a single art group (2.51 million visitors in 2025).
artworks.relevance: Demonstrates how bodily immersion and physical interaction (water, floor surfaces) can be primary material for generative art. The visitor's body becomes part of the artwork's computation.

artworks.title: Universe of Water Particles / Flowers and People
artworks.description: Water simulated as hundreds of thousands of particles following physics-based computation; flowers bloom and scatter seasonally in response to visitor proximity. Real-time rendering means the visual state is always unique.
artworks.relevance: Exemplifies art-as-substrate where natural phenomena are computationally modeled and human presence modulates the generative system. The seasonal cycle shows how temporal data feeds can drive artistic change.
